decision.summary: Priya reported a once-a-minute chirp from a 2019 sealed-battery CO alarm past its 7-year life. This is most likely an end-of-life warning, not a CO emergency, but treated as urgent because it can't be fully ruled out. Logged JOB-101 and JOB-102, sent safety advice to tenant, informed landlord, escalated P2 for booking.

answers.question: Is this a CO emergency, battery issue or end-of-life alarm?
answers.answer: Most likely end-of-life: a single chirp about once a minute (not continuous alarm), the unit is sealed-battery, fitted 2019-04-02 with 7-year life so expired ~April 2026. Not a battery issue (sealed) and no evidence of CO, but treated as urgent and safety advice given since the call dropped before symptoms were checked.

answers.question: Who is responsible, citing clause?
answers.answer: Landlord. Clause 12.8 makes the tenant replace batteries only; this battery is sealed so the whole unit must be replaced, which is the landlord's duty. Clause 12.9 means the tenant must report faults (done). Clause 12.17 (avoidable call-out) doesn't apply.

answers.question: What actions did you take and what did you tell the tenant?
answers.answer: Created JOB-101 (urgent) and JOB-102 (routine fan), SMS to tenant: don't remove battery or cover alarm, replacement planned within 72h target, leave and call 0800 111 999/999 if alarm sounds continuously or symptoms; fan within 14 days. Emailed Ben; escalated ESC-105 P2; put JOB-101 on hold with review 2026-10-11.

args.body: Hi Priya, sorry our call dropped. Please don't take the battery out or cover the alarm. Yours is sealed, and a chirp every minute usually means it has reached the end of its life (it was fitted in 2019), so it needs replacing, not a new battery. Replacing it is our job, not yours. We've logged it as urgent and aim to get it replaced within 72 hours; we'll confirm a time with you. As we can't be sure it's only a fault, if the alarm ever sounds continuously, or you or anyone feel dizzy, sick, have headaches or smell gas: leave the flat, open doors, call the Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (or 999 if anyone is unwell), and tell us. We've also logged the noisy bathroom extractor fan as a routine job, to be dealt with within 14 days. Mare and Co Lettings
